newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mozambique selling 300 to 400 state firms - minister.
newsitem.headline: Mozambique selling 300 to 400 state firms - minister.

text.p: Several hundred state businesses are to be sold in 1997 in Mozambique's privatisation programme, Industry, Trade and Tourism Minister Oldemiro Baloi said in an interview published on Saturday.
The partially state-owned Noticias newspaper quoted Baloi as saying 300 to 400 businesses would be privatised this year, bringing to an end the programme which began in 1989.
Most of the enterprises are small businesses taken over by the state shortly after independence from Portugal in 1975.

Many of the original owners, mostly of Portuguese origin, fled as civil war raged between the government and Renamo rebels supported by the white governments ruling South Africa and then-Rhodesia. The fighting ended in 1992.
About 700 companies had already been sold off, Baloi said, adding that 90 percent of privatised firms had been sold to Mozambicans.
Economic analysts said the most important companies had come under the control of foreign investors.

Last year 51 percent of the country's largest bank, the Banco Comercial de Mocambique, was sold to a Portuguese-led consortium and two state-owned breweries were earlier sold to Indol International BV, a Dutch subsidiary of South African Breweries.
Investors from Britain, Denmark, Zimbabwe, Swaziland and Mauritius are among those that have bought interests in firms sold off by the state.
Mozambican President Joaquim Chissano said earlier this month that the privatisation programme would continue, though he did not detail which enterprises would be put up for sale.
The programme has been strongly criticised by left-wing members of the ruling Frelimo party.
